newsitem.title: UK: Copper powers higher again on heavy covering.
newsitem.headline: Copper powers higher again on heavy covering.

text.p: Copper prices extended earlier gains in brisk afternoon trade on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, surging to a two-month high of $2,035 a tonne, up $76, or four percent, from Thursday's close.
Floor traders said one ring dealing member was covering large tonnages of short positions it had adopted earlier on the expectation that prices would fall.
Copper powers higher again on heavy =2
Fuelling the move higher were minor supply disruptions at a copper mine in Chile and a copper smelter in Namibia.
With global copper stocks still low, supply scares tend to have an exaggerated influence over the price, traders explained.
"This is heavy short-covering by one quarter in particular," said one LME trader.
Copper prices have now recovered by 17 percent from the 18-month low of $1,745 hit in June following revelations that Japanese giant Sumitomo Corp lost $1.8 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
